thread:
maria: Heads up — us-west-2 serving pool 3 saw a sustained throughput drop starting 07:12 UTC. Multiple workers restarted, we saw GPU OOMs and throughput fell ~40%. Dashboards show p95 latency doubled. Notified here first.

ashwin: I pulled logs from node-gpu-17. Seeing repeated `cudaOutOfMemoryError` from the allocator at the same time as a KV cache thrash. KV eviction rate spiked ~3x at 07:12.

lia: Is this noisy-tenant limited or a kernel-fallback loop? Any kernel-switch traces to correlate?

ashwin: Yes — kernel selection trace shows fastpath -> fallback -> fallback -> fastpath loops for some model variants, ~8 switches/sec on affected GPUs. Batching throughput dropped, coalescer queue length increased. Quick flame/top hotspots: 

```
alloc_slab_sweep: 34%
kv_cache_lookup: 18%
kernel_compat_check: 12%
batch_coalesce: 10%
other decoding / memcpy ops: remainder
```

Also seeing decoding_worker OOM stack traces. p99 latency jumped from ~1.2s to ~3.6s.

kevin: Confirmed on heap histograms — lots of small pinned allocations and fragmentation. My suspicion: allocator fragmentation + repeated kernel fallback causes extra allocations and evictions which then cause cascaded OOMs and worker restarts.

maria: Can we do a quick mitigation to stop the bleed? Reduce batch sizes, disable aggressive fallback, or throttle noisy tenants?

lia: Propose immediate canary: set `runtime.batch.max_tokens` from 4096 -> 2048, set `kernel.fallback.enabled=false` to prevent oscillation, and lower `coalescer.max_latency_ms` from 15 -> 8 to force smaller, more predictable batches. Apply to 5% subset first.

kevin: I can push a hotfix via config manager. Command I'll run: 

```
rctl rollout set-config --pool us-west-2 --subset 5%
  --set "runtime.batch.max_tokens=2048"
  --set "kernel.fallback.enabled=false"
  --set "coalescer.max_latency_ms=8"
```

Rolling now.

deploy-bot: rollout started: runtime-config-hotfix -> pool us-west-2 subset 5% (ids: canary-1347).

sre-oncall: Watching metrics. If p95 doesn't improve within 10m revert. Also add memory-sampling profiler on canary nodes (heap + slab fragmentation sampling).

(10 minutes later)

sre-oncall: Canary update: p95 down from 3.6s -> 1.1s, throughput on canary +18%, no OOMs observed. Evict rate on canary down ~70%.

ashwin: Kernel-switch events dropped to near-zero on canary. Heap fragmentation persists but is less acute; immediate pressure relieved. We'll expand rollout and follow up with allocator fixes.

maria: Action items: 1) Expand canary to 25% now. 2) Ashwin to open PR for allocator fastpath defragmentation and slab reuse. 3) Lia to add permanent sampling profiler + new alert for KV-evict surge. 4) Write postmortem doc with timeline and mitigations.

lia: Created internal ticket INF-4872 with profiling blobs and suggested patch. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4891 (draft).

kevin: Expanding rollout to 25%.

deploy-bot: rollout update: runtime-config-hotfix now at 25% (canary-1347, canary-1348, canary-1349).

sre-oncall: Observability looks stable on rollout subset. We'll keep the incident open until allocator PR lands and full rollout completes.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll start the postmortem timeline and sync with support for customer impact notes.

kevin: Follow-up note: we should also add a short-term heuristic to avoid kernel fallback when free-devmem < 10% to prevent oscillation. I'll include that in the PR.

ashwin: Will attach heap snapshots and kernel selection traces to the INF ticket.

lia: I'll add the KV-evict surge as an alert with runbook steps (throttle noisy tenant, reduce batch, rollback config).

maria: Thanks everyone — keeping incident channel open for final closure.
